answer: Every ballot's price is drawn in an atlas anyone can read — Harberger's self-assessed tax, the Sound Dues' 1–2% toll, the Crown free to buy cargo at its declared value. A farm stamping 10,000 ballots dies by the buyout check: price each at $0.10 and a stranger buys the whole farm for $1,000; price each at $25 and a 7% yearly tax plus a $25 bond locks $250,000 and bleeds $17,500 a year. Re-pricing each tide needs a fresh 20-minute proof of life. At the zenith of the market, every price is written in umber ink — and a farm priced at $0.10 loses all 10,000 ballots for $1,000.
